title: The Parish of Greywater Bay
premise: Elodie Blackwood, the reclusive archivist of Greywater Bay Cathedral, is pulled into a murder investigation when a drowned woman is found in the locked crypt wearing clothes stolen from Elodie's own closet. As Detective Inspector Sable Okafor works the case, Elodie realizes the killer is following the blueprint of a decades-old scandal buried in the parish records—a cover-up that made Elodie's found family of clergy and caretakers rich, and made Elodie's late mentor its architect. When a second body appears dressed in another archivist's stolen clothes, Elodie understands the killer is punishing the keepers of the secret in order of complicity, and that Elodie is next. In the climax, Elodie uses the crypt's own locking mechanism to trap the killer—the forgotten ward of the parish, cheated of her inheritance—and chooses to unseal the full record, destroying the institution that sheltered him but finally claiming a family built on truth rather than silence.
about_author: Emrys Pemberton is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent eleven years cataloguing the quiet cruelties of coastal church towns before turning to fiction. They write from a converted vestry on the northern coast, where the tide still dictates their working hours.

chapters.title: The Tide Keeps Its Own Ledger
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A quiet morning cataloguing deeds is shattered by a scream from the crypt stairs. The body of Verity Marsh, parish benefactor, lies in the sealed crypt wearing Elodie's own grey cardigan. Emotional beat: the violation of a man whose invisibility was his armor, now publicly marked.

chapters.title: A Detective with Salt in Her Hair
chapters.summary: Sable Okafor's POV. The DI arrives to find a crypt locked for forty years, one key, and an archivist who answers questions with citations. She notes Elodie's clothes match the corpse's. Emotional beat: mutual suspicion sharpened into grudging professional respect.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Searching the archive for Verity's recent visits, Elodie finds pages razored from the 1979 parish ledger—the year the Blackwood bequest was founded. Emotional beat: the first crack in his belief that the parish's kindness was uncomplicated.

chapters.title: Everyone in Greywater Owes Someone
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Interviews paint Verity as beloved and feared: she controlled the parish's charitable trust, and three staff members recently asked her for money. Emotional beat: the detective sees a web of dependency where the town sees charity.

chapters.title: Clothes That Remember
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Forensics confirm the cardigan was taken from Elodie's locked vestry flat. Only five people have keys. Elodie begins a private list, hating himself for suspecting the people who raised him. Emotional beat: loneliness of a found family under audit.

chapters.title: The Ward Nobody Claims
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Records reveal a child placed in the parish's care in 1978, officially 'relocated,' whose trust fund was absorbed into the Blackwood bequest. The file is thin—too thin. Emotional beat: the cold arithmetic of institutional mercy.

chapters.title: Father Ambrose Confesses Nothing
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie confronts the elderly canon who mentored him, who deflects with scripture and then, quietly, begs him to let the dead stay buried. Emotional beat: love and complicity braided together; the mentor's fear is real.

chapters.title: Second Clothes, Second Body
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The sexton is found drowned in the baptismal font, wearing the stolen cassock of a long-dead archivist. The pattern is now unmistakable: the killer is reenacting a list. Emotional beat: dread hardening into method.

chapters.title: The Order of Drowning
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Cross-referencing the stolen garments with the mutilated ledger, Elodie reconstructs the sequence: the victims die in the order their names appear on the 1979 cover-up document. His mentor's name is third. Emotional beat: the archive becomes a countdown.

chapters.title: What the Bequest Bought
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Following the trust money, she finds the bequest funded the cathedral's restoration—and the silence of four officials who certified a child's death that never happened. Emotional beat: power revealed as a purchased quiet.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Was Declared Dead
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie locates the ward's true trail: she survived, was passed between institutions, and wrote letters to the parish for years—all returned unopened, all still in a box Elodie himself catalogued. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger, and horror at his own hands in her erasure.

chapters.title: A Name in the Margins
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The letters were signed with a childhood nickname; Okafor traces it to a living parish employee—someone with keys, access, and a forty-year grievance. Emotional beat: the suspect list collapsing to one aching possibility.

chapters.title: The Confession Elodie Wrote
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie discovers his own mentor authored the falsified death certificate, and that the 'found family' that took Elodie in was bought with the ward's stolen inheritance. Emotional beat: identity shattered—his belonging was the crime's proceeds.

chapters.title: Night Watch
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. She moves to protect the third name on the list, but Father Ambrose has locked himself in the crypt with the records, determined to burn them. Emotional beat: a good man choosing damnation to protect the living.

chapters.title: Fire in the Undercroft
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie reaches Ambrose first and trades the truth he wants—the full story, witnessed—for the ledger. Ambrose dies that night, peacefully, in his chair. Emotional beat: inheritance of guilt formally passed to the next generation.

chapters.title: The Killer Makes Contact
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A note in the archive, in the ward's handwriting, invites Elodie to the crypt: 'You of all people know what a record is worth. Come read the last entry.' Emotional beat: terror and recognition—the killer sees him as a fellow keeper of records.

chapters.title: Sable Draws the Line
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Okafor forbids Elodie from going; Elodie goes anyway, leaving her the reconstructed ledger as insurance. Emotional beat: trust broken deliberately, as an act of protection.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. In the crypt, Elodie meets the ward—now the parish's unassuming flower-arranger—who has spent a lifetime watching her murderers prosper. She offers Elodie a choice: die as the record's final name, or help her finish it. Emotional beat: the seduction of righteous vengeance.

chapters.title: The Lock That Turns Both Ways
chapters.summary: Climax. Elodie's POV. Elodie pretends to join her, then springs the crypt's counterweight lock—the same mechanism that sealed the original crime—trapping her with the evidence as Okafor arrives. Emotional beat: the archivist weaponizes the archive; mercy and betrayal in one motion.

chapters.title: What We Do With the Truth
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The killer, unrepentant, forces the town to hear the 1979 record read aloud at her hearing. Okafor must decide whether the cover-up's surviving beneficiaries face charges. Emotional beat: justice as an open wound, honestly dressed.

chapters.title: Unsealed
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie publishes the full record, ending the bequest and the cathedral's patronage—his found family's foundation, dismantled by his own hand. Some never speak to him again. Emotional beat: the cost of truth, paid without flinching.

chapters.title: A Parish of the Living
chapters.summary: Resolution. Elodie's POV. A year on, a smaller parish rebuilds around the archive, now open to the public; the ward's letters are exhibited under her true name. Okafor brings Elodie a cold case file, unofficially. Emotional beat: a family chosen in daylight at last, and a door left open for the next mystery.
